abstract: Mitochondrial complex I translocates protons through hydrated channels whose connectivity and electrostatics are both defined by structure, but whether they are distinctly constrained is unknown. From a 2.39 cryo-EM structure modelling 2,945 ordered waters, we built the proton wire of the seven mtDNA-encoded ND subunits and scored all 40,166 missense substitutions on two near-orthogonal axes (r = 0.17): electrostatic shift at proton-loading sites, and topological disruption of the wire. Across 858 germline variant sites, loading sites (0.51) and cut vertices (0.67) are both depleted. In tumours only loading sites are enriched (1.42 TCGA, 1.67 PCAWG, 1.29 MSK-IMPACT), a 3.06-fold difference tested as a wire class tissue-type interaction (P = 3.6 10-). It survives adjustment for conservation, burial and coverage, and is concentrated in ND1 within 15 of the quinone cavity, not spread along the proton path. Selection separates charge from connectivity, without establishing a fitness benefit.
